title: Extension by zero of modules along the inclusion of an open subscheme: left adjoint to restriction, with stalks
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U\subseteq X$ an open subscheme with inclusion $j:U\to X$, so that $\mathcal O_U(W)=\mathcal O_X(W)$ for $W\subseteq U$ open. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] let $\mathcal G|_U$ be the $\mathcal O_U$-module $W\mapsto\mathcal G(W)$ ($W\subseteq U$ open) with the restriction maps of $\mathcal G$, and for a morphism $\psi$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules let $\psi|_U=(\psi_W)_{W\subseteq U}$ [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. For an $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal F$ let $j_{p!}\mathcal F$ be the presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on $X$ with $(j_{p!}\mathcal F)(V)=\mathcal F(V)$ if $V\subseteq U$ and $(j_{p!}\mathcal F)(V)=0$ if $V\not\subseteq U$ ($V\subseteq X$ open), $\mathcal O_X(V)$ acting on $\mathcal F(V)=\mathcal F(V)$ through $\mathcal O_X(V)=\mathcal O_U(V)$ when $V\subseteq U$; the restriction map along $V'\subseteq V$ is the restriction map of $\mathcal F$ if $V\subseteq U$ and $0$ otherwise. A morphism $\alpha:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ gives $j_{p!}\alpha$, equal to $\alpha_V$ for $V\subseteq U$ and $0$ otherwise. Let $\theta_{\mathcal F}:j_{p!}\mathcal F\to j_!\mathcal F$ be the sheafification of $j_{p!}\mathcal F$ as a presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], and $j_!\alpha$ the morphism induced by $j_{p!}\alpha$; $j_!\mathcal F$ is the *extension of $\mathcal F$ by zero*. Then: (1) $j_!:\Mod(\mathcal O_U)\to\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ is an additive functor; (2) $j_!$ is left adjoint to restriction: for every $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal F$ and every $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ the map $\Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(j_!\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\to\Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G|_U)$, $\psi\mapsto(\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F})|_U$, is bijective, and natural in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$; (3) for $x\in X$ with stalks as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]: if $x\notin U$ then $(j_!\mathcal F)_x=0$; if $x\in U$ then the map $\mathcal F_x\to(j_!\mathcal F)_x$, $s_x\mapsto(\theta_{\mathcal F,V}(s))_x$ ($V\subseteq U$ an open neighbourhood of $x$, $s\in\mathcal F(V)$), is well defined and an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules, natural in $\mathcal F$ (for $\alpha:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ it carries $\alpha_x$ to $(j_!\alpha)_x$).

source.place: Sheaves, Lemma 00A7 (label lemma-j-shriek-modules, line 4771) parts (2) and (3), with the definition of extension by zero for modules in Definition 00A4 (label definition-j-shriek-structures, line 4612) parts (1), (2), (5), (6), in Section 009Z (label section-open-immersions); the abelian case is Lemma 00A5 (label lemma-j-shriek-abelian, line 4685). The proofs there are 'Omitted'; the set-valued analogue is Lemma 00A3 (label lemma-j-shriek).

proof.text:
*Step 1 ($j_{p!}$ on presheaves of modules).* Let $\mathcal F$ be an $\mathcal O_U$-module. The rule for $j_{p!}\mathcal F$ is well defined: if $V'\subseteq V$ and $V\subseteq U$ then $V'\subseteq U$, so the restriction $\mathcal F(V)	o\mathcal F(V')$ lands in $(j_{p!}\mathcal F)(V')$; if $V
ot\subseteq U$ the source is $0$ and the map is $0$. For $V''\subseteq V'\subseteq V$ the composite of the restrictions is the restriction along $V''\subseteq V$: for $V\subseteq U$ these are restrictions of $\mathcal F$, and for $V
ot\subseteq U$ both maps start at $0$; restriction along $V\subseteq V$ is the identity in both cases. So $j_{p!}\mathcal F$ is a presheaf of abelian groups. Each $(j_{p!}\mathcal F)(V)$ is an $\mathcal O_X(V)$-module: for $V\subseteq U$ through $\mathcal O_X(V)=\mathcal O_U(V)$, for $V
ot\subseteq U$ the zero module. A restriction along $V'\subseteq V$ is semilinear over $\mathcal O_X(V)	o\mathcal O_X(V')$: for $V\subseteq U$ this is the semilinearity of the restriction of the $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal F$ over $\mathcal O_U(V)	o\mathcal O_U(V')$, which is the restriction of $\mathcal O_X$, and for $V
ot\subseteq U$ the map is $0$ out of $0$. So $j_{p!}\mathcal F$ is a presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For $\alpha:\mathcal F	o\mathcal F'$ the family $j_{p!}\alpha$ ($\alpha_V$ for $V\subseteq U$, $0$ otherwise) commutes with restrictions (for $V\subseteq U$ by the naturality of $\alpha$, otherwise both composites start at $0$) and is $\mathcal O_X(V)$-linear on each $V$ (since $\alpha_V$ is $\mathcal O_U(V)$-linear [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]); so it is a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules. Sectionwise one reads off $j_{p!}( eta\alpha)=j_{p!} eta\circ j_{p!}\alpha$, $j_{p!}(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$ and $j_{p!}(\alpha+\alpha')=j_{p!}\alpha+j_{p!}\alpha'$ (morphisms are added sectionwise).

proof.text: *Step 2 (clause (1): $j_!$ is an additive functor).* By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] the presheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules $j_{p!}\mathcal F$ (Step 1) has a sheafification $\theta_{\mathcal F}:j_{p!}\mathcal F\to j_!\mathcal F$, an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map to a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules through which every $\mathcal O_X$-linear map from $j_{p!}\mathcal F$ to a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules factors uniquely. For $\alpha:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ the map $\theta_{\mathcal F'}\circ j_{p!}\alpha:j_{p!}\mathcal F\to j_!\mathcal F'$ is $\mathcal O_X$-linear with target a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules, so there is exactly one morphism $j_!\alpha:j_!\mathcal F\to j_!\mathcal F'$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules with $j_!\alpha\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}=\theta_{\mathcal F'}\circ j_{p!}\alpha$ (this is the 'induced morphism' of the statement). Functoriality: $j_!\beta\circ j_!\alpha$ and $j_!(\beta\alpha)$ both satisfy $(-)\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}=\theta_{\mathcal F''}\circ j_{p!}(\beta\alpha)$ by Step 1, and $\mathrm{id}$ satisfies the condition for $j_!(\mathrm{id})$, so uniqueness gives $j_!(\beta\alpha)=j_!\beta\circ j_!\alpha$ and $j_!(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$. Additivity: the Hom sets of $\Mod(\mathcal O_X)$ are abelian groups under sectionwise addition and composition is biadditive [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; hence $(j_!\alpha+j_!\alpha')\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}=\theta_{\mathcal F'}\circ j_{p!}\alpha+\theta_{\mathcal F'}\circ j_{p!}\alpha'=\theta_{\mathcal F'}\circ j_{p!}(\alpha+\alpha')$ (Step 1), and uniqueness gives $j_!(\alpha+\alpha')=j_!\alpha+j_!\alpha'$.

proof.text:
*Step 3 (the adjunction on the presheaf level).* Let $\mathcal F$ be an $\mathcal O_U$-module and $\mathcal G$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module, with its restriction $\mathcal G|_U$, an $\mathcal O_U$-module [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. Let $\Phi:\Hom_{\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O_X)}(j_{p!}\mathcal F,\mathcal G)	o\Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G|_U)$, $\varphi\mapsto\varphi|_U=(\varphi_W)_{W\subseteq U}$: for $W\subseteq U$ open, $\varphi_W:\mathcal F(W)=(j_{p!}\mathcal F)(W)	o\mathcal G(W)=(\mathcal G|_U)(W)$ is $\mathcal O_X(W)=\mathcal O_U(W)$-linear, and for $W'\subseteq W\subseteq U$ the restriction maps of $j_{p!}\mathcal F$ and of $\mathcal G|_U$ are those of $\mathcal F$ and of $\mathcal G$, so $\varphi|_U$ commutes with them; it is a morphism of $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Conversely, for $a:\mathcal F	o\mathcal G|_U$ let $	ilde a_V=a_V$ for $V\subseteq U$ and $	ilde a_V=0:0	o\mathcal G(V)$ for $V
ot\subseteq U$. Each $	ilde a_V$ is $\mathcal O_X(V)$-linear. For $V'\subseteq V$: if $V\subseteq U$, then $V'\subseteq U$ and $	ilde a_{V'}(s|_{V'})=a_{V'}(s|_{V'})=a_V(s)|_{V'}$ by the naturality of $a$; if $V
ot\subseteq U$, both composites $(j_{p!}\mathcal F)(V)=0	o\mathcal G(V')$ are $0$. So $	ilde a$ is a morphism of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. Clearly $\Phi(	ilde a)=a$; and $\widetilde{\Phi(\varphi)}=\varphi$, since both agree at $V\subseteq U$ and at $V
ot\subseteq U$ both are maps out of the zero module, hence $0$. So $\Phi$ is bijective. It is natural: for $\alpha:\mathcal F'	o\mathcal F$, $\Phi(\varphi\circ j_{p!}\alpha)$ has components $\varphi_W\circ\alpha_W$ ($W\subseteq U$), i.e. $\Phi(\varphi\circ j_{p!}\alpha)=\Phi(\varphi)\circ\alpha$; for $\gamma:\mathcal G	o\mathcal G'$, $\Phi(\gamma\circ\varphi)=\gamma|_U\circ\Phi(\varphi)$ componentwise.

proof.text: *Step 4 (clause (2)).* Let $\mathcal F$, $\mathcal G$ be as in Step 3. By the universal property of the sheafification of presheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], $\psi\mapsto\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}$ is a bijection $\Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(j_!\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\to\Hom_{\mathrm{PMod}(\mathcal O_X)}(j_{p!}\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ ($\mathcal G$ is a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules; existence of the factorization is surjectivity, its uniqueness injectivity). Composing with the bijection $\Phi$ of Step 3 gives that $\psi\mapsto\Phi(\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F})=(\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F})|_U$ is bijective; its inverse sends $a$ to the unique $\psi$ with $\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}=\tilde a$. Naturality in $\mathcal G$: for $\gamma:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$, $((\gamma\psi)\circ\theta_{\mathcal F})|_U=\Phi(\gamma\circ(\psi\theta_{\mathcal F}))=\gamma|_U\circ(\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F})|_U$ by Step 3. Naturality in $\mathcal F$: for $\alpha:\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F$, $(\psi\circ j_!\alpha)\circ\theta_{\mathcal F'}=\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}\circ j_{p!}\alpha$ by the defining property of $j_!\alpha$ (Step 2), so $((\psi\circ j_!\alpha)\circ\theta_{\mathcal F'})|_U=\Phi(\psi\theta_{\mathcal F}\circ j_{p!}\alpha)=(\psi\circ\theta_{\mathcal F})|_U\circ\alpha$ by Step 3. Hence $j_!$ is left adjoint to $\mathcal G\mapsto\mathcal G|_U$.

proof.text: *Step 5 (stalks of $j_{p!}\mathcal F$).* Let $x\in X$; stalks, germs and the module structures on stalks are as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]: every element of a stalk is a germ, and $s_x=s'_x$ iff $s,s'$ agree on some smaller open neighbourhood of $x$. (a) If $x\notin U$, no open neighbourhood $V$ of $x$ is contained in $U$, so $(j_{p!}\mathcal F)(V)=0$ for all of them; every element of $(j_{p!}\mathcal F)_x$ is a germ of an element of $0$, so $(j_{p!}\mathcal F)_x=0$. (b) Let $x\in U$. The open neighbourhoods of $x$ in $U$ are the open neighbourhoods $V$ of $x$ in $X$ with $V\subseteq U$, and on them $\mathcal F(V)=(j_{p!}\mathcal F)(V)$ with the same restriction maps, $\mathcal O_U(V)=\mathcal O_X(V)$ likewise. Define $\lambda:\mathcal F_x\to(j_{p!}\mathcal F)_x$ by $s_x\mapsto s_x$ ($s\in\mathcal F(V)$, $x\in V\subseteq U$). Well defined: if $s_x=s'_x$ in $\mathcal F_x$, then $s|_W=s'|_W$ for an open $x\in W\subseteq U$, so the germs agree in $(j_{p!}\mathcal F)_x$. Injective: if $s_x=0$ in $(j_{p!}\mathcal F)_x$, then $s|_W=0$ for some open $x\in W\subseteq V\subseteq U$, so $s_x=0$ in $\mathcal F_x$. Surjective: an element of $(j_{p!}\mathcal F)_x$ is a germ $t_x$, $t\in(j_{p!}\mathcal F)(V)$; then $t_x=(t|_{V\cap U})_x$ and $t|_{V\cap U}\in\mathcal F(V\cap U)$, so $t_x=\lambda((t|_{V\cap U})_x)$. The same argument for $\mathcal O$ shows that $\mu:\mathcal O_{U,x}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $r_x\mapsto r_x$, is a ring isomorphism (it is compatible with sums and products of germs), and $\mathcal F_x$ is an $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-module through $\mu^{-1}$; then $\lambda(r_xs_x)=\lambda((r|_Ws|_W)_x)=r_x\lambda(s_x)$, so $\lambda$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules. For $\alpha:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$, $\lambda'(\alpha_x(s_x))=(\alpha_V(s))_x=(j_{p!}\alpha)_V(s)_x=(j_{p!}\alpha)_x(\lambda(s_x))$, so $\lambda$ is natural in $\mathcal F$.

proof.text: *Step 6 (clause (3)).* By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] the underlying sheaf of abelian groups of $j_!\mathcal F$, with $\theta_{\mathcal F}$, is the sheafification of the underlying presheaf of abelian groups of $j_{p!}\mathcal F$; so by [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-sheafification-space] the map $\theta_{\mathcal F,x}:(j_{p!}\mathcal F)_x\to(j_!\mathcal F)_x$, $s_x\mapsto\theta_{\mathcal F,V}(s)_x$, is a group isomorphism for every $x\in X$, and it is $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear since $\theta_{\mathcal F}$ is $\mathcal O_X$-linear [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. If $x\notin U$, $(j_!\mathcal F)_x\cong(j_{p!}\mathcal F)_x=0$ by Step 5(a). If $x\in U$, the map of the statement is $\theta_{\mathcal F,x}\circ\lambda$ ($s_x\mapsto\theta_{\mathcal F,V}(s)_x$ for $s\in\mathcal F(V)$, $x\in V\subseteq U$), well defined and an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules as a composite of two (Step 5(b)). Naturality: for $\alpha:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$, taking stalks of $j_!\alpha\circ\theta_{\mathcal F}=\theta_{\mathcal F'}\circ j_{p!}\alpha$ (Step 2; stalks of a composite are the composite of stalks, by the formula $s_x\mapsto\varphi(s)_x$) gives $(j_!\alpha)_x\circ\theta_{\mathcal F,x}=\theta_{\mathcal F',x}\circ(j_{p!}\alpha)_x$, and with the naturality of $\lambda$ (Step 5) $(j_!\alpha)_x\circ(\theta_{\mathcal F,x}\lambda)=(\theta_{\mathcal F',x}\lambda')\circ\alpha_x$.
